subject: SLA commitments, action owners, and QBR-ready executive brief
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem summary + owners (Acme incident 2026-02-26)

Team —

Quick summary from the on-call findings for the Acme incident on 2026-02-26 (downtime window ~18m, token-serving rate spike >4x for 12m):

- Root cause: API gateway health-check misrouting combined with a model-variant cache miss storm; fallback routing saturated a small pool.
- Customer impact: elevated latencies (95th moved from 120ms to ~1.8s) and failed streamed responses for ~3% of requests; Acme reported visible degradation on their search assistant.
- Immediate containment: scaled dedicated pool + emergency routing rule (11:03–11:30 PST).

I've attached a compact postmortem (acme_postmortem_summary.pdf) and a candidate SLO revision/mitigation runbook (slo_runbook_v2.md). Key action items I've assigned below — please confirm owners and ETA by Wed EOD so we have a QBR-ready executive slide.

Action items (initial owners / suggested ETA):
1) Route hardening: add health-check parity & fallback throttles — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: 2026-03-12
2) Model cache warming for high-churn variants — owner: Jonas Weber (infra) + SRE — ETA: 2026-03-08
3) Observability: token-level tracing for gateway handoffs — owner: Laura Bennett — ETA: 2026-03-05
4) Customer comms + credit proposal: coordinate with sales/CS — owner: Vivek Kulkarni — ETA: 2026-03-04

For the QBR: we need a one-slide executive synopsis (cause, impact, remediation, customer outcome, and ask). If we can lock owners/ETAs and the attached one-pager by Thu I'll finalize.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_postmortem_summary.pdf (2 pages), slo_runbook_v2.md (draft)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Postmortem summary + owners (Acme incident 2026-02-26)

Jonas — thanks for the crisp deck. A couple of exec asks to prepare the QBR-ready slide: 

- Quantify customer-visible harm in business terms (search failures -> estimated lost sessions / SLA credit calc). Marissa, can you work with Amit to pull a 30-day delta for affected endpoints?
- Risk posture: what's the probability this exact sequence recurs within 90 days if we only apply the runbook? Laura, include a short residual risk line.
- Credits ask: propose a dollar or % credit range; I'll route to finance but need a recommended figure.

Also flagging that Acme is evaluating Dedicated capacity expansion next quarter — this will be a negotiating point if we don't show tightened controls. I want the one-slide to include: impact number, root-cause sentence, top 3 mitigations, and next customer-facing milestone. Keep it tight (5 bullets).

I'll draft an executive blurb once you confirm the numbers.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Customer Success & Revenue
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2026 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Postmortem summary + owners (Acme incident 2026-02-26)

Looping in a couple of data points we pulled with Amit:

- Customer-visible metric: the affected search endpoint showed ~2.1k failed streams during the 18-minute window; estimated lost sessions ~1.6k (based on our session-success mapping).
- SLA exposure: projected credit range (if applied per contract): $6k–$12k depending on partial vs. full-window credit.
- Customer sentiment: Amit said Acme will hold off on an immediate expansion decision but expects a remediation timeline before their Q3 contract review.

Updates on action items: 
- Route hardening: PR submitted to gateway repo, awaiting SRE review (links: https://github.com/redwood/gateway/pull/432). ETA for deploy to prod: 2026-03-10 (conservative).
- Cache warming: infra experiment shows 40% reduction in cache-miss spikes on canary — need runbook automation (Jonas team).
- Observability: Laura has a draft trace instrumentation plan; requesting permission for a short production opt-in for Acme traffic next week.

I'll prepare a short slide with the numbers and the proposed credit band for Vivek to include in the exec blurb.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: qbr_onepager_SLA_table.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Postmortem summary + owners (Acme incident 2026-02-26)

Thanks all — quick confirmation for QBR packet: 

- Owners/ETAs locked: Route hardening (Marissa) 2026-03-10; Cache warming automation (Jonas + SRE) 2026-03-12; Observability trace opt-in (Laura) 2026-03-06.
- Customer comms: Vivek to lead credit proposal; Marissa will include the exact failure counts on the one-slide.
- Ask for QBR: Approve proposed credit band ($6k–$12k) and agree to include a brief timeline in the customer success play.

I'll assemble the one-slide and add to the QBR deck link (Drive) once Laura confirms the trace opt-in wording.

-Jonas

-- Forwarded conversation headers preserved as inline quotes where appropriate.

Notes: Attachments stored in shared drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4dSLA_BRIEF (exec one-pager + postmortem). JIRA ticket for action tracking: SRE-4872.
